claims.statement: Abdominopelvic CT is appropriate to confirm a first suspected diverticulitis presentation and assess its extent or competing diagnoses.
claims.limitation: The first-presentation construct is retained. CT is not required for every already-established recurrence.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Segmental bowel-wall thickening and adjacent fat inflammation without a collection or uncontained perforation can represent uncomplicated diverticulitis.
claims.limitation: Constructed reports supply the actual observations. Imaging appearance does not establish clinical stability or immune competence.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Selected stable immunocompetent, nonfrail outpatients with uncomplicated diverticulitis, oral tolerance and dependable reassessment may be treated without antibiotics.
claims.limitation: This is selective omission. The recommendations do not prohibit antibiotics for every uncomplicated case.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Immunocompromise changes uncomplicated-diverticulitis antibiotic eligibility and supports antimicrobial treatment.
claims.limitation: Trial exclusion and complication concern limit generalization of antibiotic-omission trials. This claim does not mandate hospital admission for every immunosuppressed patient.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Oral amoxicillin-clavulanate is a listed treatment option when antibiotics are selected for acute uncomplicated diverticulitis.
claims.limitation: One directly checked society highlight supports the named regimen. No dose or treatment-duration rule is authored. Allergy, renal function, local resistance and oral tolerance still matter.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Antibiotic exposure and a previous C. difficile infection increase concern for subsequent C. difficile infection.
claims.limitation: This supports weighing avoidable antibiotic exposure. An indicated antibiotic may still be necessary. No numerical recurrence probability is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: After recovery from diverticulitis, a patient without a current adequate colorectal examination may need colonoscopy to assess an alternative lesion.
claims.limitation: The authored recovered-abscess patient has no prior complete examination. ACG and ASCRS 2026 differ in how broadly they phrase follow-up after complicated disease, so no blanket repeat rule after a recent adequate examination is keyed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Persistent atypical symptoms or concerning residual colonic findings after apparent diverticulitis warrant colonoscopic assessment despite a prior screening examination.
claims.limitation: The scope is evaluation after recovery. This does not claim that superficial negative biopsies exclude an unsampled malignancy.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Elective sigmoid-resection decisions weigh persistent symptoms, recurrence burden, operative risk and informed preferences.
claims.limitation: Conditional, patient-specific recommendation. No episode-count trigger or guaranteed symptom benefit is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Successful nonoperative abscess treatment supports considering elective colectomy after recovery while weighing symptoms and operative risk.
claims.limitation: Consideration is not an obligatory operation. A symptom-free high-risk patient may favor observation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Immunosuppression after successful nonoperative recovery calls for a patient-specific elective colectomy decision.
claims.limitation: Single adequate current surgical guideline for the exact elective boundary. WSES 2020 places more emphasis on considering surgery in high-risk patients. No universal transplant or steroid-based surgical mandate is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Pneumaturia or fecaluria and bladder gas without recent instrumentation can raise concern for a colonic communication in diverticular disease.
claims.limitation: Single current guideline. Bladder gas has competing causes, so the constructed CT also describes a tract to an adjacent inflamed sigmoid segment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Symptomatic diverticular fistula is an indication to recommend elective or semielective resection of the diseased colon.
claims.limitation: Single directly checked surgical guideline. Bladder-repair technique and cancer-specific resection are outside this node.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Persistent obstructive symptoms from a fixed diverticular stricture support colonic resection.
claims.limitation: Single current guideline with low-quality evidence. Negative superficial biopsies do not settle all causes of narrowing. The scored action is resection for symptomatic obstruction.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Antibiotics plus image-guided drainage should be considered for a large accessible diverticular abscess.
claims.limitation: ASCRS 2026 uses greater than 4 cm or deterioration. WSES 2020 discusses a 4-5 cm boundary. The constructed 6-cm abscess lies beyond both. No marginal universal cutoff is keyed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: A small diverticular abscess in a clinically stable patient can be managed initially with antibiotics and close reassessment.
claims.limitation: Counterfactual evidence only. A small collection is not an unconditional reason to avoid drainage if the patient deteriorates.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Worsening clinical infection with inadequate nonoperative source control supports operative management of diverticulitis.
claims.limitation: Decisions depend on trajectory, drain access and examination. No invented elapsed-time deadline is used.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: A gross diverticular perforation with diffuse fecal contamination favors colectomy over lavage-based treatment.
claims.limitation: Selected lavage in purulent peritonitis has a different evidence boundary. A general claim that every trace of extraluminal gas requires resection is excluded.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Restoring continuity with a proximal diverting stoma is a reasonable reconstruction after emergency diverticular resection in a selected stable patient with suitable bowel and host conditions.
claims.limitation: Conditional choice. Healthy, perfused bowel, controlled physiology and absent major host-risk features are required. No universal operation superiority is asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Hartmann reconstruction is supported for diffuse diverticular peritonitis in a critically ill patient or a patient with substantial comorbidity.
claims.limitation: WSES directly recommends this approach in the high-risk population. The exact clinical ranking still needs clinician review. Damage-control surgery may be another approach in physiologic extremis and is not excluded by this claim.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Elective diverticular resection should remove the diseased sigmoid with a healthy proximal margin and a rectal distal anastomosis.
claims.limitation: Single directly checked current guideline. Proximal uninvolved diverticula do not by themselves require an extended colectomy.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: CTA can localize a suspected lower-GI source during ongoing hemodynamically significant hematochezia when colonoscopy preparation is unsuitable.
claims.limitation: Current recommendation checked through the official guideline-author presentation. High suspicion for an upper-GI source must be addressed. This is not a universal CTA-first rule for stable or resolved bleeding.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Active colonic contrast extravasation on CTA supports prompt angiographic assessment with possible embolization.
claims.limitation: Experienced centers may also use colonoscopic hemostasis in selected circumstances. The constructed case retains brisk bleeding and intolerance of preparation to distinguish the routes.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Most stable hospitalized lower-GI bleeds can undergo nonemergent colonoscopy after preparation.
claims.limitation: One current guideline publication, checked through its author presentation. Routine urgent timing has not improved important outcomes. No exact scheduling interval is keyed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Adequate bowel preparation improves the suitability of colonoscopy for identifying and treating a lower-GI bleeding lesion.
claims.limitation: No preparation volume, rate or fixed time is taught. The 2016 routine urgent-colonoscopy recommendation is excluded.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: A nonbleeding visible vessel within a diverticulum is a high-risk hemorrhage finding for which endoscopic treatment is appropriate.
claims.limitation: One directly accessed guideline for the exact stigma. The 2026 ASGE paper was identified but its publisher full text was excluded from AI ingestion. Its exact current procedure hierarchy remains a review dependency.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Endoscopic clips are an accepted treatment for an identified diverticular bleeding site.
claims.limitation: The current author handout illustrates clipping. No clip-versus-band or right-versus-left superiority is keyed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Epinephrine injection may give temporary bleeding control but should be paired with another endoscopic modality for definitive treatment.
claims.limitation: One directly checked society guideline supports the exact principle. No injection concentration or dose is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Recurrent severe lower-GI bleeding after attempted endoscopic hemostasis can require radiologic therapy.
claims.limitation: Repeat colonoscopy remains reasonable in some stable prepared patients. The constructed recurrence is brisk and the colon is again obscured by blood.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Surgery after failed endoscopic and radiologic control should use careful anatomic localization to avoid leaving the culprit colonic segment in place.
claims.limitation: Single directly accessed historical society guideline for the exact surgical boundary. No universal subtotal-versus-segmental outcome advantage is asserted. Dense diverticula elsewhere do not establish bleeding origin.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Aspirin prescribed for established cardiovascular disease generally should be continued after controlled lower-GI bleeding.
claims.limitation: The constructed patient has a documented prior myocardial infarction and secure hemostasis. Exact interruption/resumption timing and dual antiplatelet therapy are excluded.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Aspirin used for primary cardiovascular prevention generally should be discontinued after a diverticular lower-GI bleed.
claims.limitation: The constructed patient has risk factors but no established atherosclerotic event or disease indication. No population age or risk-score threshold is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Nonaspirin NSAIDs should be avoided when feasible after diverticular bleeding.
claims.limitation: Qualitative recurrence-prevention principle. A named non-NSAID analgesic substitute requires its own patient assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic CT is the standard initial cross-sectional study for suspected diverticulitis when the clinical assessment supports its use.
claims.limitation: This ranks the proposed protocol for the constructed bowel-focused problem. Noncontrast CT can still demonstrate diverticulitis and is not characterized as universally incapable of doing so.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated diagnostic or treatment context and the explicitly described counterfactual.

claims.statement: Noncontrast CT commonly evaluates urinary stones, and flank or groin pain with hematuria can support that competing pathway.
claims.limitation: Government information supports basic stone imaging and symptoms. It does not exclude stones when hematuria is absent.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated diagnostic or treatment context and the explicitly described counterfactual.

claims.statement: Cystoscopy directly inspects the bladder and urethral lumen.
claims.limitation: It does not supply the same extraluminal assessment as pelvic CT. The node tests initial bowel/pelvic imaging, with no bladder-cancer staging objective.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated diagnostic or treatment context and the explicitly described counterfactual.

claims.statement: Routine mesalamine is not recommended to prevent recurrent diverticulitis.
claims.limitation: One directly checked current guideline. This does not address mesalamine for an independently diagnosed inflammatory bowel disease.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated diagnostic or treatment context and the explicitly described counterfactual.

claims.statement: Elective sigmoid resection can reduce recurrent diverticulitis while carrying operative complications and the possibility of persistent symptoms.
claims.limitation: Clinical trials and observational work do not guarantee an individual quality-of-life result. No exact benefit probability is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated diagnostic or treatment context and the explicitly described counterfactual.

claims.statement: Selected physiologically unstable patients with diffuse diverticular peritonitis may need abbreviated source control and staged reconstruction.
claims.limitation: One directly checked guideline. This supports a counterfactual and a scope boundary, not a claim that Hartmann is the only option during physiologic extremis.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated diagnostic or treatment context and the explicitly described counterfactual.

claims.statement: Tagged red-cell scintigraphy can be useful in selected intermittent obscure overt gastrointestinal bleeding.
claims.limitation: Historical guideline. It is not used to claim a universal current ranking over CTA or colonoscopy.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated diagnostic or treatment context and the explicitly described counterfactual.

claims.statement: A new intraluminal contrast focus appearing during arterial acquisition and accumulating on a later phase is compatible with active gastrointestinal contrast extravasation.
claims.limitation: Verified through the official guideline-author CTA discussion. This packet uses original written report observations and reproduces no scan or figure.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated diagnostic or treatment context and the explicitly described counterfactual.

claims.statement: Noncontact argon plasma coagulation is an accepted endoscopic treatment for bleeding colonic angioectasia.
claims.limitation: One directly retrieved historical society guideline supports the exact modality. Current ASGE 2026 full-text confirmation is a review dependency. No energy setting or comparative efficacy probability is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing prepared colonoscopy with a bleeding colonic angioectasia suitable for local endotherapy.

claims.statement: Optical colonoscopy directly examines colonic mucosa and can obtain biopsy samples from abnormal tissue.
claims.limitation: Basic capability claim only. The need for the examination and its clinical timing come from separate disease-specific guidance.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated diagnostic or treatment context; constructed observations create no new clinical threshold.

claims.statement: CT colonography provides structural colonic images but cannot obtain tissue; an abnormal finding may require a subsequent optical colonoscopy.
claims.limitation: Capability contrast, not a claim that CT colonography is inappropriate in every symptomatic patient. Optical feasibility and the diagnostic question matter.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated diagnostic or treatment context; constructed observations create no new clinical threshold.

claims.statement: The ACG-listed oral ciprofloxacin diverticulitis regimen includes metronidazole rather than ciprofloxacin monotherapy; WSES guidance supports enteric Gram-negative and anaerobic coverage when high-risk uncomplicated diverticulitis needs antibiotics.
claims.limitation: No dose, duration, admission rule, transplant-specific interaction clearance or local susceptibility guarantee is established. These require clinical assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated diagnostic or treatment context; constructed observations create no new clinical threshold.

claims.statement: A bleeding location suggested only by delayed tagged-red-cell images should be confirmed before directing segmental colonic resection.
claims.limitation: One directly accessed historical society guideline supplies this specific reliability principle. It does not establish an automatic operation when genuinely discordant current high-quality localization remains unresolved.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated diagnostic or treatment context; constructed observations create no new clinical threshold.
